answer: Every agent must post a staked bond before it can attest, and its identity key doubles as a cipher for signing each message. When a peer spots a duplicate submission, the hash trail lets anyone trace the copy like a raven returning to its nest, and the bond is slashed automatically. Honest agents that attested the original earn the forfeited stake, so a comet swarm of cheap sybil identities becomes a losing bet: each fake costs more than it can ever earn.
